Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Owner-streamed Godot bodies

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use Body2 for cooperative motion produced by a Godot solver and accepted through Replay's entity-ownership protocol. It borrows a RigidBody2D or CharacterBody2D and an optional skin node. Its driver and visual smoothing live outside simulation state.

Odin
body2_attach(&adapter, physics_body, .Rigid, skin)
body2_sync(&adapter, authority_owned_state, my_owner_id, epoch,
           authority_tick, may_publish, render_delta, optional_observer_state)
sample, error := body2_sample(&adapter, engine_physics_frame)

The ownership argument must come from authority state, not client prediction. session_authority_state supplies the appropriate frame. Connection/fencing/game eligibility is a separate may_publish decision. Optional observed history may interpolate a remote pose only within the same object/revision/discontinuity scope. Observers freeze rigid bodies in kinematic mode; remote character bodies remain solid but their local controller must not call move_and_slide. body2_simulating answers whether a controller may operate the local solver.

Transforms are written through PhysicsServer and the node's global transform; linear/angular velocity and sleeping state cross reseeds. Freeze is lifted before seeding a new solver, avoiding Godot restoring an obsolete pose when it wakes. Temporary Variants are destroyed. Samples read PhysicsServer state and reuse the last immutable observation between physics frames, so differing render/network rates do not erase the newest observation. Character samples use real velocity.

Preparing an authority-issued offer can run a speculative solver while the old owner remains accepted. body2_preview can start a local-only possession preview earlier; it publishes nothing until an authority offer exists. Matching preparation can retain the preview, while denial, cuts, lost eligibility and timeout revert it. There may be overlapping speculative solvers. Exactly one revision is accepted by the owner-state reducer at a time.

Node reseeds are immediate; a frozen kinematic PhysicsServer transform may settle on the next physics step. Skin rendering therefore reads the visible parent node, while publication reads the solver. Small position/angular corrections decay on the skin with a 63 ms half-life; explicit cuts reset both errors and do not glide. The visual-only skin is a direct child with a captured authored offset/rotation. Observer jumps of at least six position units or 0.12 radians trigger correction; 90-unit or π/2-radian corrections cut. Scene geometry/scale is authored separately from the streamed pose. The adapter does not serialize solver contact caches, joints, or arbitrary engine state. Reconstructing pose and velocity is a cooperative recovery boundary, not deterministic solver replay. The current skin-offset correction assumes unit global body scale; scaled hierarchy visual correction needs separate validation. The physics pose uses global transforms.

body2_destroy only clears the adapter; the caller owns and frees the nodes. When a current authority frame is unavailable, call body2_suspend to stop solving and publication while retaining the previous observation clock. Do not tag a cached old-world pose with the new session epoch: a recovered checkpoint may have an earlier tick. Resume with the actual authority frame so the driver can rebase its scope and seed the complete recovered pose and velocities. For 3D, Body3 applies the same owner protocol to quaternion poses and linear/angular velocity; a separate Replay Slopball3D port exercises it.
